conclusions: The morphism $f$ is a closed immersion.
hypotheses: A morphism $f:Z\to X$ of locally ringed spaces; an open cover $X=\bigcup U_i$ such that each $f^{-1}(U_i)\to U_i$ is a closed immersion.
statement:
Let $f : Z \to X$ be a morphism of locally ringed spaces.
In order for $f$ to be a closed immersion it suffices
that there exists an open covering $X = \bigcup U_i$ such
that each $f : f^{-1}U_i \to U_i$ is a closed immersion.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: There exists a submodule $N\subset M$ such that $S^{-1}N=N'$.
hypotheses: A module $M$ and a multiplicative subset $S$ of its base ring; a submodule $N'\subset S^{-1}M$.
statement:
Any submodule $N'$ of $S^{-1}M$ is of the form $S^{-1}N$ for some
$N\subset M$. Indeed one can take $N$ to be the inverse image of
$N'$ in $M$.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: The category of schemes has a final object, products, and fibre products; equivalently, it has finite limits.
hypotheses: The category of schemes.
statement:
The category of schemes has a final object, products and fibre products.
In other words, the category of schemes has finite limits, see
Categories, Lemma \ref{categories-lemma-finite-limits-exist}.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

hypotheses: A finite Jacobson space.
A Jacobson space with finitely many closed points.
statement:
A finite Jacobson space is discrete.
A Jacobson space with finitely many closed points is discrete.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

hypotheses: A finite Jacobson space.
A Jacobson space with finitely many closed points.

conclusions: Its prime spectrum is a spectral space.
hypotheses: A ring.
statement:
The spectrum of a ring is a spectral space, see Topology, Definition
\ref{topology-definition-spectral-space}.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: The representable functor $h_T$ is an algebraic space.
hypotheses: A scheme $T$.
statement:
A scheme is an algebraic space. More precisely,
given a scheme $T \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
the representable functor $h_T$ is an algebraic space.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: Two polynomials in $k[x]$ are relatively prime.
They have no common root in an algebraic closure of $k$.
equivalence_sides: Two polynomials in $k[x]$ are relatively prime.
They have no common root in an algebraic closure of $k$.
hypotheses: Two polynomials in $k[x]$ are relatively prime.
They have no common root in an algebraic closure of $k$.
statement:
Two polynomials in $k[x]$ are relatively prime precisely when they
have no common roots in an algebraic closure $\overline{k}$ of $k$.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: The first is equivalent to the opposite of the second, via global sections of the structure sheaf.
hypotheses: The category of affine schemes and the category of rings.
statement:
The category of affine schemes is equivalent to the opposite of the
category of rings. The equivalence is given by the functor that associates
to an affine scheme the global sections of its structure sheaf.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: It belongs to $V_\alpha$ for some ordinal $\alpha$.
hypotheses: An arbitrary set.
statement: Every set is an element of $V_\alpha$ for some ordinal $\alpha$.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

hypotheses: A ring $R$ and three $R$-modules $M,N,P$.
statement:
For any three $R$-modules $M, N, P$,
$$
\Hom_R(M \otimes_R N, P) \cong \Hom_R(M, \Hom_R(N, P))
$$
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

hypotheses: A finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring.
A localization of a Noetherian ring.
statement:
Any finitely generated ring over a Noetherian ring
is Noetherian. Any localization of a Noetherian ring
is Noetherian.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: Its underlying topological space is locally quasi-compact.
hypotheses: A scheme.
statement:
The underlying topological space of any scheme is
locally quasi-compact, see
Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-locally-quasi-compact}.

statement:

to another scheme is separated.
